--- language: - en - zh license: other license_name: tencent-hy-world-2.0-community license_link: https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-World-2.0/blob/main/License.txt pipeline_tag: image-to-3d library_name: hy-world-2 tags: - worldmodel - 3d - hy-world extra_gated_eu_disallowed: true ---

HY-World 2.0: A Multi-Modal World Model for Reconstructing, Generating, and Simulating 3D Worlds

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README_zh.md)


"What Is Now Proved Was Once Only Imagined"

## 🎥 Video https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b56f4750-25c9-48fb-83ff-d58526711463 ## 🔥 News - **[May 18, 2026]**: 🤗 Open-source World Generation inference code and WorldStereo 2.0 model weights! - **[May 11, 2026]**: 🤗 Open-source HY-Pano 2.0 inference code and model weights! - **[April 16, 2026]**: 🚀 Release HY-World 2.0 technical report & partial codes! - **[April 16, 2026]**: 🤗 Open-source WorldMirror 2.0 inference code and model weights! ## 📋 Table of Contents - [📖 Introduction](#-introduction) - [✨ Highlights](#-highlights) - [🧩 Architecture](#-architecture) - [📝 Open-Source Plan](#-open-source-plan) - [🎁 Model Zoo](#-model-zoo) - [🤗 Get Started](#-get-started) - [🔮 Performance](#-performance) - [🎬 More Examples](#-more-examples) - [📚 Citation](#-citation) ## 📖 Introduction **HY-World 2.0** is a multi-modal world model framework for **world generation** and **world reconstruction**. It accepts diverse input modalities — text, single-view images, multi-view images, and videos — and produces 3D world representations (meshes / Gaussian Splattings). It offers two core capabilities: - **World Generation** (text / single image → 3D world): syntheses high-fidelity, navigable 3D scenes through a four-stage method —— a) ![Panorama Generation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Panorama_Generation-4285F4?style=flat-square) with HY-Pano 2.0, b) ![Trajectory Planning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Trajectory_Planning-EA4335?style=flat-square) with WorldNav, c) ![World Expansion](https://img.shields.io/badge/World_Expansion-FBBC05?style=flat-square) with WorldStereo 2.0, and d) ![World Composition](https://img.shields.io/badge/World_Composition-34A853?style=flat-square) with WorldMirror 2.0 & 3DGS learning. - **World Reconstruction** (multi-view images / video → 3D): Powered by WorldMirror 2.0, a unified feed-forward model that simultaneously predicts depth, surface normals, camera parameters, 3D point clouds, and 3DGS attributes in a single forward pass. HY-World 2.0 is an **open-source state-of-the-art** world model. We released all model weights, code, and technical details to facilitate reproducibility and advance research in this field. ### Why 3D World Models? Existing world models, such as Genie 3, Cosmos, and HY-World 1.5 (WorldPlay+WorldCompass), generate pixel-level videos — essentially "watching a movie" that vanishes once playback ends. **HY-World 2.0 takes a fundamentally different approach**: it directly produces editable, persistent 3D assets (meshes / 3DGS) that can be imported into game engines like Blender/Unity/Unreal Engine/Isaac Sim — more like "building a playable game" than recording a clip. This paradigm shift natively resolves many long-standing pain points of video world models: | | Video World Models | 3D World Model (HY-World 2.0) | |--|---|---| | **Output** | Pixel videos (non-editable) | Real 3D assets — meshes / 3DGS (fully editable) | | **Playable Duration** | Limited (typically 1 min) | Unlimited — assets persist permanently | | **3D Consistency** | No (flickering, artifacts across views) | Native — inherently consistent in 3D | | **Real-Time Rendering** | Requires per-frame inference; high latency | Consumer GPUs can render in real time | | **Controllability** | Weak (imprecise character control, no real physics) | Precise — zero-error control, real physics collision, accurate lighting | | **Inference Cost** | Accumulates with every interaction | One-time generation; rendering cost ≈ 0 | | **Engine Compatibility** | ✗ Video files only | ✓ Directly importable into Blender / UE / Isaac Engine | | | $\color{IndianRed}{\textsf{Watch a video, then it's gone}}$ | $\color{RoyalBlue}{\textbf{Build a world, keep it forever}}$ |

All above are real 3D assets (not generated videos) and entirely created by HY-World 2.0 -- captured from live real-time interaction.

## ✨ Highlights - **Real 3D Worlds, Not Just Videos** Unlike video-only world models (e.g., Genie 3, HY World 1.5), HY-World 2.0 generates **real 3D assets** — 3DGS, meshes, and point clouds — that are freely explorable, editable, and directly importable into **Unity / Unreal Engine / Isaac**. From a single text prompt or image, create navigable 3D worlds with diverse styles: realistic, cartoon, game, and more.

- **Instant 3D Reconstruction from Photos & Videos** Powered by **WorldMirror 2.0**, a unified feed-forward model that predicts dense point clouds, depth maps, surface normals, camera parameters, and 3DGS from multi-view images or casual videos in a single forward pass. Supports flexible-resolution inference (50K–500K pixels) with SOTA accuracy. Capture a video, get a digital twin.

- **Interactive Character Exploration** Go beyond viewing — **play inside your generated worlds**. HY-World 2.0 supports first-person navigation and third-person character mode, enabling users to freely explore AI-generated streets, buildings, and landscapes with physics-based collision. Go to [our product page](https://3d.hunyuan.tencent.com/sceneTo3D) for free try (![Very Crowded Now](https://img.shields.io/badge/Very_Crowded_Now,_Be_Patient-EA4335?style=flat-square)).

## 🧩 Architecture - **Refer to our tech report for more details** A systematic pipeline of HY-World 2.0 — *Panorama Generation* (HY-Pano-2.0) → *Trajectory Planning* (WorldNav) → *World Expansion* (WorldStereo 2.0) → *World Composition* (WorldMirror 2.0 + Splattings Learning) — that automatically transforms text or a single image into a high-fidelity, navigable 3D world (3DGS/mesh outputs).

## 📝 Open-Source Plan - [x] Technical Report - [x] WorldMirror 2.0 Code & Model Checkpoints - [x] Full Inference Code for World Generation (WorldNav + WorldStereo + World Composition) - [x] Panorama Generation (HY-Pano 2.0) Model & Code - [x] World Expansion (WorldStereo 2.0) Model & Code ## 🎁 Model Zoo ### World Reconstruction — WorldMirror Series | Model | Description | Params | Date | Hugging Face | |-------|-------------|--------|------|--------------| | WorldMirror-2 [new] | Multi-view / video → 3D reconstruction | ~1.2B | 2026 | [Download](https://huggingface.co/tencent/HY-World-2.0/tree/main/HY-WorldMirror-2.0) | | WorldMirror-1 | Multi-view / video → 3D reconstruction (legacy) | ~1.2B | 2025 | [Download](https://huggingface.co/tencent/HunyuanWorld-Mirror/tree/main) | ### Panorama Generation — HY-Pano Series | Model | Description | Params | Date | Hugging Face | |-------|-------------|--------|------|--------------| | HY-Pano-2 [new] | Text / image → 360° panorama | ~80B | 2026 | [Download](https://huggingface.co/tencent/HY-World-2.0/tree/main/HY-Pano-2.0) | | HY-Pano-2-Qwen [new] | Text / image → 360° panorama | ~425M | 2026 | [Download](https://huggingface.co/tencent/HY-World-2.0/blob/main/HY-Pano-2.0/pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors) | ### World Expansion — WorldStereo Series | Model | Description | Params | Date | Hugging Face | |-----------------|-------------|-----|------|--------------| | WorldStereo-2 [new] | Panorama → 3DGS world | ~17B | 2026 | [Download](https://huggingface.co/hanshanxue/WorldStereo/tree/main) | We recommend referring to our previous works, [WorldStereo](https://github.com/FuchengSu/WorldStereo) and [WorldMirror](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanWorld-Mirror), for background knowledge on 3D world generation and reconstruction. ## 🤗 Get Started ### Install Requirements We recommend **CUDA 12.8** and **Python 3.11+**. The easiest path is to prepare one shared environment, first make **World Reconstruction (WorldMirror 2.0)** work, and then install the extra components required by **World Generation**. #### 1. Create the shared environment ```bash git clone https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-World-2.0 cd HY-World-2.0 conda create -n hyworld2 python=3.11.15 conda activate hyworld2 ``` #### 2. Install World Reconstruction dependencies After this step, the environment is ready for **worldrecon / WorldMirror 2.0**. ```bash # Base dependencies shared by worldrecon and worldgen pip install -r requirements.txt # Recommended: install the custom gsplat variant once for both worldrecon and worldgen cd hyworld2/worldgen/third_party/gsplat_maskgaussian pip install -e . --no-build-isolation cd ../../../../ ``` If you only need **worldrecon** and want a simpler fallback, official `gsplat` is also supported: ```bash pip install git+https://github.com/nerfstudio-project/gsplat.git ``` Install **one** FlashAttention backend: ```bash # Recommended for Hopper GPUs: FlashAttention-3 git clone https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention.git cd flash-attention/hopper python setup.py install cd ../../ rm -rf flash-attention ``` ```bash # Simpler alternative: FlashAttention-2 pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation ``` #### 3. Add extra World Generation dependencies Run the following extra steps only if you need **worldgen**. These commands assume the shared `hyworld2` environment above is already active. ```bash # Git-based dependencies require torch/CUDA to be installed first pip install --no-build-isolation -r requirements_git.txt # recastnavigation is managed as a git submodule git submodule update --init --recursive # Recast navmesh extension for trajectory planning cd hyworld2/worldgen/third_party/navmesh pip install . --no-build-isolation cd ../../../../ ``` For **HY-Pano-2** installation, please refer to **[hyworld2/panogen/README.md](hyworld2/panogen/README.md)**. ### Code Usage — Panorama Generation (HY-Pano-2) For full documentation and CLI reference, see **[hyworld2/panogen/README.md](hyworld2/panogen/README.md)**. We provide a `diffusers`-like Python API for HY-Pano 2.0. Model weights are automatically downloaded from Hugging Face on first run. ```python from pipeline import HunyuanPanoPipeline pipeline = HunyuanPanoPipeline.from_pretrained('tencent/HY-World-2.0') output = pipeline('input.png') output.save('output_panorama.png') ``` ### Code Usage — World Generation (WorldNav, WorldStereo-2, and 3DGS) The world Generation pipeline turns a panorama scene into a navigable 3D world through five stages: | Stage | Script | Description | |-------|--------|-------------| | 1. Trajectory Planning | `traj_generate.py` | VLM-guided camera trajectory planning with obstacle-aware navigation | | 2. Trajectory Rendering | `traj_render.py` | Multi-GPU point-cloud rendering along planned trajectories | | 3. World Expansion | `video_gen.py` | WorldStereo-2 keyframe generation with memory-guided consistency | | 4. GS Data Preparation | `gen_gs_data.py` | Extract frames, aligned depth, normals, and cameras for 3DGS training | | 5. 3DGS Training | `world_gs_trainer.py` | Optimize and export the final Gaussian Splatting world | For full documentation, prerequisites, and CLI arguments, see **[hyworld2/worldgen/README.md](hyworld2/worldgen/README.md)**. ### Code Usage — WorldMirror 2.0 WorldMirror 2.0 supports the following usage modes: - [Code Usage](#code-usage--worldmirror-20) - [Gradio App](#gradio-app--worldmirror-20) We provide a `diffusers`-like Python API for WorldMirror 2.0. content.text:
Blunt answer: **no.** Nobody can make all of level 5 exactly your approved picture, with Benny swimming freely through real 3D and zero blur. A single painting doesn't contain the rest of the tunnel; any tool has to invent it, and invented parts are never exactly your art.

**What you can realistically have:**
1. **Very close, not exact:** a level 5 that looks very close to your screen, for as long as the 3D world holds up. Today that's 2.4 seconds. The Plus test shows whether it can be longer.
2. **Short Screen 05:** make Screen 05 the good section only, then go straight into Screen 06. That's real 3D, looks like your art, and is honest. It's just short.
3. **Hire a 3D artist:** for the whole level, hire a 3D environment artist to build the tunnel by hand using your picture as the guide. That's how real games do it: very close, still not exact.

Running the Marble 1.1 Plus test now, with your approval. It costs 1,580–3,080 of your existing 3,610 credits, no cash; World Labs decides the exact amount during the job. The project's safety check was still capped at your November budget, so I'm updating it to your approval today. It will still refuse any job that could cost more than your balance.

definition.description:
Withdraw a task suggestion you queued earlier with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion has gone stale: the issue was fixed in this session (by you or the user), it turned out not to be a problem after all, or you have queued a better-scoped replacement — in that case queue the replacement with spawn_task first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only a suggestion the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn. If they already started, dismissed or edited it, the result says so and nothing changes; that answer is final, so don't retry or re-flag it.

Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", don't start it anew, and do it here only if the user asks for that in chat.

reason.description: Optional short note on why the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34". It doesn't change the outcome.

task_id.description: The task_id from the spawn_task result that queued the suggestion (of the form task_1a2b3c4d).

definition.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task

definition.description:
Suggest a separate task for something you noticed that is outside the scope of your current work.

Call this when you come across something that deserves fixing but doesn't belong in this change — dead code, stale docs, a missing test, a confirmed TODO, a bug or security issue spotted in passing. Don't use it for trivial fixes you can make inline, for anything the user asked you to do, for vague code-smell impressions or unverified hunches, or to split off parts of your own task. The call only queues a suggestion and returns; carry on with your current work.

The user sees a "Suggested task" card in the Claude desktop app with your title and tldr, can open the full prompt, and with one click starts it as a new session — on their machine in their local clone of this repository (optionally a fresh worktree of it), or in the cloud — sends it to this session, or dismisses it. A new session starts from your prompt alone, on a checkout that may not have this session's changes, so the prompt has to stand alone: what to change and why, the files involved by repository-relative path, and any context from this conversation it depends on. Absolute paths and other state of this environment may not exist there. If the find involves a secret or credential, say where it is rather than copying the value, since the prompt is stored and displayed.

The result carries a task_id; if the suggestion later becomes moot, withdraw it with dismiss_task.

prompt.description: The opening message of the new session: the goal, the files involved by repository-relative path, the context it needs from this conversation, and what done looks like. The user can read it in full before starting; markdown is fine. Keep it to what the task needs (hard limit 32000 characters) — the new session can read the code itself.

title.description: The card's heading and the new session's title: a short imperative phrase starting with a verb, under 60 characters, that makes sense on its own — e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option".

tldr.description: One or two plain sentences on what the task would do and why it is worth doing. Shown on the card under the title; it is what the user reads when deciding whether to start it, so no file paths or code.

definition.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task

targetFrames.description: The views to generate, in output order, returned in `frames`: one posed frame per view. Each target frame requires a `camera` at 1280x720 with pinhole intrinsics. refinePoses.description: Bundle-adjust the estimated cameras against dense matches before answering. The backbone's poses are good to about half a degree, which is enough to reconstruct from and not enough to refine against: the residual shows up as blur wherever two views disagree. The solve anchors on the depth this task has just produced, so it costs a matcher pass and a solve rather than another reconstruction, and it needs two or more frames. A solve that moves the cameras further than the guards allow is thrown away and the unrefined reconstruction is returned, which is a success rather than an error.
refinePoses.title: Refineposes

targetResolution.description: Return the depth, confidence and camera intrinsics on this (width, height) pixel grid: one of 1280 by 720, 720 by 1280, 960 by 720 or 528 by 704, the grids the depth model serves. The reconstruction is scaled to cover the requested size and center-cropped to it, so the result is exactly the size asked for and never stretched, and the intrinsics are updated with it -- unprojecting the returned depth with the returned camera gives the same geometry either way. A requested aspect that differs from the frames' costs field of view, since the crop is what makes the size exact, and centroidWorld then describes the cropped view. Omit it (or pass null) and a multi-view capture with camera translation comes back on whichever of those four grids is closest in aspect to the frames: smaller frames are scaled up onto it, and other aspects (square or 3:2, for example) are center-cropped onto the closest one, with squares going to 960 by 720. A single image or a capture without camera translation comes back on the reconstruction backend's native grid. Set it when a later step needs a particular grid: atlasGenerate, for example, needs context frames with the same aspect as its target cameras.
targetResolution.title: Targetresolution

entries.name: mcp__Marble_World_Labs__posedImages2Splats

entries.description: Convert Gaussian splats, such as posedImages2Splats returns, into a GLB mesh with an optional texture or vertex colors. Uses the project's World Labs Developer API credits. Returns an operation immediately; poll get_operation for the result. Reuse the same idempotency_key when retrying so the work is not submitted twice. Guide: https://docs.atlas.worldlabs.ai/api-reference/splats2-mesh.md

CamerasAutoAnchors.description:
Find anchor positions automatically, then render from them.

Candidates come from the free space the geometry encloses, and `oriented`
picks which rule judges one valid. The default when a request names no
cameras.

oriented.description: Judge a candidate by whether the surface faces it, which needs splats whose normals are oriented -- usually only true if they were optimized for it. Leave false to judge by enclosure alone, which is safe on any scene.
oriented.title: Oriented

CamerasAutoAnchors.title: CamerasAutoAnchors

CamerasExteriorSphere.description:
Render from a sphere around the splats, looking inward.

For anything whose surface can be seen from outside -- an object, a turntable
capture -- no anchors are needed. Cameras are spread evenly over a sphere
bounding the splats and aimed at its center. Naming an
`orientedBoundingBox` sizes that sphere on the splats inside it, which is
what picks one object out of a larger capture.
CamerasExteriorSphere.title: CamerasExteriorSphere

CamerasManualAnchors.description:
Render from explicitly placed anchor positions.

A cubemap is rendered at each anchor, and more cameras are sampled around
it. Anchors belong in open space, with a clear view of the regions that
matter most.

anchors.description: Anchor positions in Three.js coordinates (+X right, +Y up, -Z forward).
anchors.title: Anchors

CamerasManualAnchors.title: CamerasManualAnchors

CoordinateFrame.description:
Pose represented by a position and an XYZW quaternion.

``coordinate_system`` names the axes convention the pose is expressed in:
``rub`` (right-up-back, the OpenGL/Three.js convention) or ``rdf``
(right-down-forward, the OpenCV convention). Both the ``coordinateSystem``
(camelCase) and ``coordinate_system`` spellings are accepted.
CoordinateFrame.title: CoordinateFrame

PinholeCamera.description:
A posed pinhole camera.

The axes convention of the pose is carried by
``extrinsics.coordinate_system``.
PinholeCamera.title: PinholeCamera

PinholeCameraIntrinsics.description:
Pinhole camera intrinsics in pixel coordinates (not normalized).

Pixel coordinates have their origin (0, 0) at the top-left corner of the
image, +x right and +y down, so ``cx``/``cy`` measure from the top-left.
``width`` and ``height`` are the image size in pixels the intrinsics
refer to. This is independent of the pose's ``coordinate_system``.
PinholeCameraIntrinsics.title: PinholeCameraIntrinsics

Splats2MeshAdvancedOptions.description: Advanced reconstruction controls for custom mesh generation.

depthSource.description: Depth of the main views. `render` uses the splats' rendered depth; `stereo` measures it by stereo matching each view against a second render from a camera shifted sideways, which is sharper where the splats are fuzzy and slower to compute. Pixels stereo cannot match keep the rendered depth.
depthSource.title: Depthsource

normalSource.description: Normals orient the implicit surface the mesh is extracted from. `depth` estimates them from the rendered depth; `render` aggregates the splats' own, which assumes each splat's local z axis points along the surface normal.
normalSource.title: Normalsource

renderHw.description: Height and width of the main views rendered to measure the splat surface and texture it, in pixels.
renderHw.title: Renderhw

renderHwSecondary.description: Height and width of the secondary views, in pixels. The anchor strategies place extra cameras from the anchors and render them here, covering what the main views miss. `exterior_sphere` and a supplied camera list render no secondary views and ignore this.
renderHwSecondary.title: Renderhwsecondary

resolution.description: Resolution of the grid the implicit surface is built on, across the region's longest side. Powers of two only. This sets the finest detail the mesh can carry.
resolution.title: Resolution

trimQuantile.description: Drop vertices whose sample density falls below this quantile. Reconstruction closes the surface over regions it saw no samples in, and trimming cuts that invented skin back off. 0 keeps every vertex.
trimQuantile.title: Trimquantile

Splats2MeshAdvancedOptions.title: Splats2MeshAdvancedOptions

Splats2MeshColliderBoxOptions.description: Collider boxes to fit to the extracted mesh.

heightAlignVoxels.description: Tolerance, in voxels, for aligning heights: neighbouring box tops (and bottoms) within it of each other are raised to a shared height, so floors stay flat to walk on. A voxel is the mesh's longest side divided by `advancedOptions.resolution`. 0 keeps the fitted heights.
heightAlignVoxels.title: Heightalignvoxels

targetBoxes.description: Maximum number of boxes. Fewer boxes enclose the mesh more loosely.
targetBoxes.title: Targetboxes

Splats2MeshColliderBoxOptions.title: Splats2MeshColliderBoxOptions

Splats2MeshOrientedBoundingBox.description: Region to extract, as an oriented box in Three.js coordinates.

center.description: Center of the region, in world space.
center.title: Center

halfExtents.description: Half the region's size along each of its own axes. All three must be positive.
halfExtents.title: Halfextents

orientation.description: Rotation of the region away from the world axes, as an xyzw quaternion.
orientation.title: Orientation

Splats2MeshOrientedBoundingBox.title: Splats2MeshOrientedBoundingBox

TaskAsset.description:
Media named by asset id, inline base64, or public URL.

A task response names each output by id and url together: the url expires,
the id does not. The pair is accepted as input as well, so a response can
be handed straight back to the next task; the id names the media and the
url is ignored. Inline base64 stands alone. A response returns it only
when a task is answered at submission; the stored operation names the
same output by id and url.

base64.description: Base64-encoded media bytes, with or without a data URL prefix. Decoded size must be less than 10 MiB. A task response carries inline bytes only when it is returned from the submission; the stored operation names the same output by `assetId` and `url`.
base64.title: Base64

url.description: Public HTTP(S) URL containing the media. On a task response this is a read URL for `assetId` and it expires; mint a fresh one with `assets/{asset}:createReadUrl`.
url.title: Url

TaskAsset.title: TaskAsset

idempotency_key.description: A unique string you choose for this request and reuse on retries of it.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

advancedOptions.description: Finer control over how the splats are rendered and how the surface is extracted. Omit for the defaults.

cameras.description: Cameras the splats are rendered from. The surface is reconstructed from those renders, so geometry no camera sees is not meshed. Name a strategy -- `auto_anchors` (the default) finds viewpoints in the scene's free space, `manual_anchors` takes them from the request, `exterior_sphere` rings the scene from outside for an object or turntable capture -- or pass a list of cameras to render as given, at most 512, sharing one width and height between 64 and 1024 that becomes the render resolution.
cameras.title: Cameras

colliderBoxes.description: Also fit oriented boxes that enclose the mesh, for collision. The boxes stay upright, turning only about the vertical axis, and come back as a second GLB asset with one node per box. Omit to skip them.

orientedBoundingBox.description: Region to extract, as an oriented box in Three.js coordinates. Omit to mesh the whole scene.

purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.description: Purge this operation's outputs and the transient uploads it consumed one hour after it finishes. Omitted, the account's setting applies; true raises it for this operation; false is refused when the account already purges. Uploads in the library are never purged by an operation.
purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.title: Purgecontentonoperationcompletion

splatAsset.description: The Gaussian splat scene (.spz) to mesh. Inline base64 must carry a `data:` prefix to declare its media type: asset creation otherwise infers the type from the bytes, and the sniffer knows image formats only.

targetFaces.description: Decimate the extracted mesh to at most this many faces. A target above the extracted count does nothing. Omit to keep every face.
targetFaces.title: Targetfaces

textureMode.description: Mesh appearance: 'image_texture' projects rendered views onto a UV atlas, 'vertex_color' bakes per-vertex colors, and 'none' leaves the mesh untextured.
textureMode.title: Texturemode

textureSize.description: Height and width of the texture atlas, in pixels, for `image_texture` mode. One rendered view plus its border has to fit, so this must be at least 2% above the render size in play: the larger render bank under the anchor strategies, `renderHw` under `exterior_sphere`, or the supplied cameras' own size.
textureSize.title: Texturesize

webhookUrl.description: Where Atlas POSTs one signed task.succeeded or task.failed event when this operation finishes; retried for 24 hours. Verify the signature with the public keys at /.well-known/webhooks/jwks.json. Cannot be combined with ?wait=true. https on port 443 only, no IP literals. Developer API only.
webhookUrl.title: Webhookurl

content.text:
No, I'm not saying that. You can have a real game where Benny swims through all of Screen 05 and it looks very close to your approved art. What nobody can give you is your painting's exact pixels in every frame.

**Marble 1.1 Plus result:** a small gain only. It holds up for about 3–3.5 seconds of swimming instead of 2.4, then the river smears the same way. It cost 1,580 of your existing credits, so your balance is 2,030. No cash was spent.

**Best route I've found for the whole level: the repeating tunnel.** It cuts one section between two gold rings from the sharp part of your current Marble world and joins copies of it end to end. Your painting is itself a tunnel of identical repeating rings, so this matches your art. In the test, Benny swam 10 units (about 7 seconds) and the river, rings and walls stayed as sharp at the end as at the start, with no blur creeping in.
- **Black far end:** the end of the tunnel shows a black hole, because I only drew three pieces ahead. When I tried drawing more, the test machine couldn't load them all. A lighter version of the distant pieces should fix that.
- **Repeats:** the river pattern repeats at every ring.

**SpAItial Echo-2: it isn't installed in this session.** It's listed in Anthropic's plugin directory as "spaitial-ai", and I've put the install card above.
- **Your own key needed:** you bring your own SpAItial API key. Whether it comes with free credits depends on your SpAItial account; I can't see that.
- **To run it:** install the card, add your key, then tell me. If its tools don't show up here, a new session may be needed.
- **The test:** I'll build one world from your clean Screen 05, test forward camera movement first, then Benny with the follow-camera. You'll get the beginning, middle and end at normal speed, compared directly to Marble's 2.4 seconds. I'll say plainly whether it beats it. No cash.

Everything is saved on GitHub (commit `e9c5889`). Your approved Screen 05, both Marble worlds and every gameplay version are unchanged.

content.content:
## API Reference

### Authentication

The SpAItial Developer API uses bearer tokens. Every request must include an `Authorization` header carrying a key issued to your account.

Your API key is a secret

Keys are shown to you exactly once at creation. Store them in a secret manager, never commit them, and never ship them inside a client-side bundle.

#### Obtaining a key[​](#obtaining-a-key "Direct link to Obtaining a key")

1. Create a key in the dashboard

   Keys are created from the developer portal in the SpAItial dashboard. Each key belongs to your account and spends from the same shared credit balance used by the app.

2. Pick the right scopes

   Each key has an explicit scope set (for example `worlds:create`, `worlds:read`, `worlds:write`, `files:create`). The scope is enforced server-side; calls outside the granted scopes return `403 forbidden`. Panorama edits use `worlds:create`; listing, reading, or downloading edited panoramas uses `worlds:read`.

3. Check your credits

   World generation spends from your shared app and API credit balance. See [Credits and Billing](https://docs.spaitial.ai/api/credits-billing.md) for plan credits, purchases, and what API actions cost.

#### Key format[​](#key-format "Direct link to Key format")

Production keys look like:

```text
spt_live_abc123def456...

```

Test or sandbox keys (if your workspace has them enabled) use a different prefix. The prefix is part of the key and must be sent verbatim.

#### Sending the key[​](#sending-the-key "Direct link to Sending the key")

Pass the key in the standard `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header:

```bash
curl https://api.spaitial.ai/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer spt_live_..."

```

A request with no `Authorization` header, an unparseable header, or a revoked key returns `401 unauthorized` with the [error codes](https://docs.spaitial.ai/api/errors.md).

#### Revoking[​](#revoking "Direct link to Revoking")

Revoke any key that may have leaked from the developer portal. Revocation takes effect on the next request. To replace a key, create a new one and revoke the old one explicitly; creating a new key does not invalidate existing ones.

#### What not to do[​](#what-not-to-do "Direct link to What not to do")

Don't leak your keys

* Do not put API keys in client-side code, mobile apps, or anything shipped to end users. Calls must be made from a server you control.
* Do not commit keys to source control. Add them to your environment or secret manager.
* Do not share a single key across unrelated services — keys are also the unit of rate limiting and observability.


---

### Mobile capture

Echo 3 turns a phone scan of a real space into a Gaussian splat world at real-world scale. You send one ZIP of frames, or [several ZIPs](#capture-multi-scan) when a space took more than one scan, and the world is ready in 30 minutes to 2 hours. Camera poses are optional, but include them when you have them.

Any capture app works as long as it produces the format below. If you'd rather not start from scratch, you can reuse our open-source [capture prototype](https://github.com/spaitial-ai/spaitial-capture-prototype), which already exports valid ZIPs.

#### Endpoints[​](#endpoints "Direct link to Endpoints")

Camera poses are optional, but include them when you have them.

Any capture app works as long as it produces the format below. If you'd rather not start from scratch, you can reuse our open-source [capture prototype](https://github.com/spaitial-ai/spaitial-capture-prototype), which already exports valid ZIPs.

content.content:
#### Upload a file[​](#upload-a-file "Direct link to Upload a file")

Send a `multipart/form-data` request with a single `file` field:

```bash
API_KEY="[REDACTED]"

curl -sX POST "https://api.spaitial.ai/v1/files" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -F "file=@photo.jpg"

```

Successful uploads return `201 Created`:

```json
{
  "file_id": "file_abc123",
  "content_type": "image/jpeg",
  "file_size": 1843921,
  "expires_at": "2026-05-21T10:42:00.000Z"
}

```

Allowed file types are JPEG, PNG, WebP, and GIF. The maximum file size is 25 MB. The API checks the detected MIME type from the file bytes, not just the uploaded filename or form content type.

#### Use the file in a world request[​](#use-the-file-in-a-world-request "Direct link to Use the file in a world request")

Pass the `file_id` as the world input:

```bash
FILE_ID=$(curl -sX POST "https://api.spaitial.ai/v1/files" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -F "file=@photo.jpg" | jq -r .file_id)

curl -sX POST "https://api.spaitial.ai/v1/worlds" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"input\": {
      \"type\": \"file_id\",
      \"file_id\": \"$FILE_ID\"
    },
    \"model\": \"echo-2\",
    \"title\": \"Uploaded kitchen reference\"
  }"

```

Using a file marks it as consumed. This is informational and visible in `GET /v1/files`; the object stays private until its lifecycle cleanup. Treat `file_id` values as one-generation inputs and upload again when you need a fresh reusable reference.

For an uploaded 360 panorama, use the same flow and add `is_pano: true` when creating the world:

```bash
PANO_FILE_ID=$(curl -sX POST "https://api.spaitial.ai/v1/files" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -F "file=@panorama.jpg" | jq -r .file_id)

curl -sX POST "https://api.spaitial.ai/v1/worlds" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"input\": {
      \"type\": \"file_id\",
      \"file_id\": \"$PANO_FILE_ID\",
      \"is_pano\": true
    },
    \"model\": \"echo-2\",
    \"title\": \"Uploaded panorama\"
  }"

```

Only set `is_pano` for equirectangular 360 panoramas. The API trusts the flag and skips suitability validation for that request.

List files owned by the current API key user:

+  far       the world beyond ring B (the tunnel end with its gold glow), placed after the last section drawn

CLAUDIA — SCREEN 05: NATURAL 3D SWIMMING AND SWIPE CONTROLS

For Level 5, Screen 05 — Flow Into the Current, I want Benny, my pink character, to move naturally through the entire 3D environment, just like a character in a polished mobile game.

Movement requirements:

1. Swipe left: Benny smoothly swims toward the left side of the river.
2. Swipe right: Benny smoothly swims toward the right side.
3. Swipe up: Benny swims upward where the environment allows vertical movement.
4. Swipe down: Benny swims downward where the environment allows it.
5. Forward movement: Benny continuously swims forward through the river and golden tunnel rings.
6. Natural animation: His body, arms, and feet should move naturally while swimming. He should gently lean when turning.
7. Smooth camera: The camera must follow Benny naturally without shaking, sudden jumps, awkward angles, or clipping through objects.
8. Clear graphics: No blurriness, black patches, stretched textures, flickering, broken geometry, or anything visually unnatural.
9. Real responsiveness: Swipes must control Benny's actual 3D position, not just play a prerecorded animation or move the background.
10. Original appearance: Preserve the approved Screen 05's river, tunnel, colors, coins, scenery, and Benny's exact character design.

Make sure Benny stays properly positioned within the river, reacts smoothly to the player's controls, and can collect coins while moving.

Most importantly: I want players to feel like they're actually controlling Benny as he swims through this beautiful environment—not watching a video.

Please test the real gameplay with repeated left, right, up, and down swipes on an Android portrait screen, and show me a continuous gameplay recording demonstrating that everything works naturally.

My goal is smooth, responsive, visually clean gameplay while maintaining approximately 90–95% likeness to my original approved Screen 05.

Real responsiveness: swipes must control Benny's actual 3D position, not a prerecorded animation or moving the background. 3. 6. Natural swim animation: keep the paddling shader; add a subtle body roll with each stroke and a stronger paddle rate while changing lanes.
7. Keep `window.step(t, dt, steer, speed)` working (steer may be ignored/overridden by lanes) and add `window.state()` returning {s, lane, lat, height, coins}.

Write `swipe_test.cjs`: Playwright chromium with SwiftShader args (copy them from track_clip.cjs), a Pixel-7-like context (viewport 412×915, deviceScaleFactor 1 to keep rendering affordable, isMobile true, hasTouch true), open `play3.html?w=412&h=915`, and drive REAL touch swipes with CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` (touchStart → several touchMove → touchEnd over ~120 ms) on the canvas: left, left, right, up, right, down, left, up. Step the game deterministically between swipes (e.g. 0.4 s of 1/30 s steps) and log `state()` after each — verify lane/lat/height respond correctly. Render ONLY 6 stills (e.g. mid lane change, top of a leap, during a dive, after collecting an air coin) as PNGs into `agentA/out_controls/`, plus `swipe_log.json`.

## Deliverables (in agentA)
`controls.js`, the edited `play3.html`, `swipe_test.cjs`, `out_controls/*.png`, `swipe_log.json`, and `CONTROLS_NOTES.md` (what you changed, exact hook lines, tuning constants, what you verified, anything not working). Report back a short summary with the file list and honest issues. Aim to finish within ~75 minutes.

input.prompt:
You are the water / visual-quality specialist on the Rainbow mobile game. Work ONLY inside this folder (your private copy):
`/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rainbow-/e7a27dfe-01e5-5ff6-9e4c-e2d0f8167a81/scratchpad/agentB`
Do NOT touch git, the repository at /home/user/rainbow- (read-only use of its files is fine), or any other folder (another specialist works in `agentA`). Do not spend any credits or call any paid API.

## What exists
`play3.html` is a standalone three.js 0.180 + Spark 2.4.0 (Gaussian-splat renderer, docs https://sparkjs.dev, types in node_modules/@sparkjsdev/spark/dist/types) page showing the user's APPROVED Screen 05 (reference picture: /home/user/rainbow-/references/05_flow_into_the_current.png — a purple perforated washer tunnel with polished gold rings, orange paddles, and a glossy cyan river with hot-pink S-shaped streaks, white foam banks, iridescent bubbles) as a 3D splat world built from a Marble (World Labs) reconstruction of that picture:
- `near.ply` = the world up to ring B; `bay.ply` / `bay_m.ply` = the sharp ring-A→ring-B section (the `_m` copy has ONLY its water/foam mirrored so the river bends the other way); `*_lo.ply` = lighter versions for distant copies; `far.ply` = the tunnel end. Copies are placed by `track.json` → `offsets` (each ring sits exactly on the previous ring) and `far_offsets`.
- Builder: /home/user/rainbow-/tools/marble05/build_track.py (+ spz.py reader/PLY writer). Rebuild into YOUR folder with:
  `python3 -I /home/user/rainbow-/tools/marble05/build_track.py /home/user/rainbow-/qa/worldlabs/05/r32/full_500k.spz /home/user/rainbow-/qa/worldlabs/05/r32/full_100k.spz scene05.json /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rainbow-/e7a27dfe-01e5-5ff6-9e4c-e2d0f8167a81/scratchpad/tile_frame.json /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rainbow-/e7a27dfe-01e5-5ff6-9e4c-e2d0f8167a81/scratchpad/rings.json <outdir> 10`
  (copy the builder into your folder before modifying it; the files near.ply etc. in your folder are symlinks into `track/`).
- Stills helper: `play_shots2.cjs` with env `PAGE=play3.html STILLS='[0,2.3,4.4,6.4]'` (`NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node play_shots2.cjs <outdir> stills`). Rendering is SOFTWARE ONLY and slow (~1–2 min per still), the machine has 4 cores shared with another specialist: render few stills, never a long clip. Never run `playwright install`.

## Your task (user's words, binding): "Making the blue-and-pink S-shaped river continuous throughout Screen 05. Making water flow naturally, with varied reflections, foam, bubbles, and splashes. Preventing visible seams, mismatched colors, glitches, and blurry areas … Clear graphics: No blurriness, black patches, stretched textures, flickering, broken geometry … Preserve the approved Screen 05's river, tunnel, colors."
1. Water flow: make the river's own splats look like flowing water toward the camera WITHOUT changing its approved colours: e.g. a Spark splat modifier (dyno / `objectModifier` / `worldModifier`) on the track meshes that, only for water splats (low height above the water plane — scene05.json `plane` n, d; or a per-splat flag you bake into a spare channel), applies a gentle moving brightness/specular ripple travelling along the river and a slight sideways shimmer; amplitude small so the streak design stays the painting's. If Spark's modifier API makes this impractical, do it with a few semi-transparent flowing highlight layers instead — explain the choice. Put it in a NEW module `waterflow.js` with minimal hook lines in `play3.html` marked `// [waterflow]`.
2. Visual cleanup of the track: (a) the small BLACK PATCHES / gaps where the water meets the walls at the sides inside the copied sections; (b) the far end currently reads as a narrower "tube inside the tube" — make the tunnel continue convincingly to its bright golden end (e.g. more distant copies drawn small with the light pieces, the far piece scaled / positioned to match the last copy's ring, or a soft golden glow); (c) any floaters or smeared splats. CLAUDIA — SCREEN 05: STRICT GAMEPLAY REQUIREMENTS — DO NOT SHOW ME AN UNFINISHED OR BROKEN RESULT

Claudia, I want to be extremely clear about what I'm asking for with Level 5, Screen 05.

I want Benny, my original pink character, to swim through the entire 3D level naturally, just like a real, professionally developed mobile game.

These are my non-negotiable requirements:

1. Smooth left and right movement: Players must be able to swipe left or right and watch Benny move naturally across the river. No jerking, teleporting, freezing, unnatural turns, or incorrect positioning.

2. Natural forward swimming: Benny must continuously move forward through the actual 3D environment. His swimming animations, body movement, turning, and camera tracking must look natural.

3. Correct upward and downward movement: Jumping, diving, and returning to the water must work smoothly without strange animations or broken positioning.

4. No visual errors: No black patches, broken tunnel sections, blurry scenery, stretched textures, flickering, missing geometry, floating objects, or unnatural water movement.

5. No gameplay errors: No crashes, freezes, collision problems, camera clipping, control failures, or broken transitions between sections.

6. Consistent approved artwork: The entire moving environment must remain as close as possible to my original approved Screen 05, including Benny, the golden tunnel, the colorful water, and the coin trail.

7. Complete gameplay testing: Test the entire level from beginning to end using actual touchscreen swipe inputs on an Android portrait device or emulator. Test repeated left and right swipes, upward and downward movement, coin collection, camera movement, and transitions.

8. Real playable 3D: Do not substitute a video, moving background, scripted character path, or prerecorded sequence for functioning gameplay.

MOST IMPORTANT — DO NOT SHOW ME A BROKEN RESULT AS FINISHED.

If Screen 05 still has errors, broken animations, crashes, blurry sections, incorrect movement, or anything that doesn't meet my requirements, do not present it to me for approval.

Instead, continue correcting and retesting the problems. You may give me a brief written progress report explaining what remains broken, but do not send another unfinished gameplay preview and ask me to approve it.

Only show me the final gameplay preview when it passes all the requirements above and you've verified it works correctly.

If you cannot achieve these requirements with the current tools or technical approach, tell me clearly what is preventing it. Do not pretend the level is finished or claim it works without testing.

I want to see Benny swimming through the full level smoothly, naturally, and without visible problems.

Once you've confirmed everything is working, save and push the completed changes to GitHub and provide the final gameplay recording and test results.

My goal is approximately 90–95% visual likeness to the original approved Screen 05, with fully functional, smooth 3D gameplay.

Do not move on to the other screens or spend additional generation credits until I approve Screen 05.

"""Per-frame visual checks for the Screen 05 acceptance run (python3 -I visual_check.py <run dir> <approved.png>):
black patches (near-black pixels below the HUD), sharpness vs the first frame (variance of the Laplacian), flicker (frame-to-frame
change spikes), and a colour-look score vs the approved picture (hue/saturation histogram overlap; motion-independent)."""
import sys, json, glob, numpy as np, cv2
d, ref = sys.argv[1:3]
files = sorted(glob.glob(f'{d}/f_*.jpg'))
R = cv2.imread(ref); R = cv2.resize(R, (412, 915))
def hs_hist(img):
    hsv = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)[150:]  # below the HUD
    h = cv2.calcHist([hsv], [0, 1], None, [36, 16], [0, 180, 0, 256]); return cv2.normalize(h, h, 1, 0, cv2.NORM_L1)
HR = hs_hist(R)
rows, prev, sharp0 = [], None, None
for f in files:
    im = cv2.imread(f); body = im[150:]
    g = cv2.cvtColor(body, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    black = float((body.max(2) < 22).mean())
    sharp = float(cv2.Laplacian(g, cv2.CV_64F).var()); sharp0 = sharp0 or sharp
    look = float(cv2.compareHist(HR, hs_hist(im), cv2.HISTCMP_INTERSECT))
    chg = float(np.abs(body.astype(np.int16) - prev).mean()) if prev is not None else 0.0
    prev = body.astype(np.int16)
    rows.append({'frame': f.split('_')[-1][:4], 'black_pct': round(100 * black, 3), 'sharpness_vs_start': round(sharp / sharp0, 3), 'colour_look_vs_approved': round(look, 3), 'change': round(chg, 2)})
chg = np.array([r['change'] for r in rows[1:]]) if len(rows) > 1 else np.array([0.0])
res = {
    'frames': len(rows),
    'black_patches': {'max_pct': max(r['black_pct'] for r in rows), 'frames_over_0_3pct': sum(r['black_pct'] > 0.3 for r in rows)},
    'sharpness_vs_start': {'min': min(r['sharpness_vs_start'] for r in rows), 'median': float(np.median([r['sharpness_vs_start'] for r in rows]))},
    'colour_look_vs_approved': {'min': min(r['colour_look_vs_approved'] for r in rows), 'median': float(np.median([r['colour_look_vs_approved'] for r in rows]))},
    'flicker': {'median_change': float(np.median(chg)), 'max_change': float(chg.max()), 'spikes_over_3x_median': int((chg > 3 * max(1e-6, np.median(chg))).sum())},
}
json.dump({'summary': res, 'frames': rows}, open(f'{d}/visual_check.json', 'w'), indent=1); print(json.dumps(res, indent=1))

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back unless the tool result says that a notice follows, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

cat > tools/marble05/sync_agents_wip.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copies (read-only) the Screen 05 specialists' in-progress work from their scratch folders into the repository so the five-minute
# autosave pushes it to GitHub: code, pages, notes, logs, test pictures, rebuilt track pieces. node_modules, symlinks and the source
# worlds (already in qa/worldlabs, qa/spaitial) are skipped. Never writes into the agents' folders.
python3 -I - <<'PY'
import os, shutil, datetime
SCR = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rainbow-/e7a27dfe-01e5-5ff6-9e4c-e2d0f8167a81/scratchpad'
DST = '/home/user/rainbow-/backups/wip/screen05-agents'
KEEP = ('.html', '.js', '.mjs', '.cjs', '.py', '.md', '.json', '.png', '.jpg', '.mp4', '.ply', '.txt', '.log')
n = 0
for a in ('agentA', 'agentB'):
    src = os.path.join(SCR, a)
    if not os.path.isdir(src): continue
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(src):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d != 'node_modules' and not d.startswith('out_run') and not os.path.islink(os.path.join(root, d))]
        for f in files:
            p = os.path.join(root, f)
            if os.path.islink(p) or not f.endswith(KEEP) or f == 'package-lock.json': continue
            if os.path.getsize(p) > 60 * 1024 * 1024: continue
            q = os.path.join(DST, a, os.path.relpath(p, src))
            if os.path.exists(q) and os.path.getmtime(q) >= os.path.getmtime(p) and os.path.getsize(q) == os.path.getsize(p): continue
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(q), exist_ok=True); shutil.copy2(p, q); n += 1
os.makedirs(os.path.join(DST, 'lead'), exist_ok=True)
for f in ('final_acceptance.cjs', 'visual_check.py'):
    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(SCR, f)): shutil.copy2(os.path.join(SCR, f), os.path.join(DST, 'lead', f))
open(os.path.join(DST, 'LAST_SYNC_UTC'), 'w').write(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() + '\n')
print('synced files:', n)
PY
EOF
bash tools/marble05/sync_agents_wip.sh; du -sh backups/wip/screen05-agents/* 2>/dev/null; find backups/wip/screen05-agents -type f | wc -l

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Round 32 → next Claude account: recreate the Screen 05 3D test workspace from the repository in one command (free, no credits).
#   bash docs/briefs/2026-11-21-r32/setup_r32.sh [workspace=/tmp/rainbow_r32]
# Creates: <ws>/base (viewer + three.js 0.180 + Spark 2.4.0 + rebuilt track), <ws>/agentA and <ws>/agentB (each specialist's newest
# saved work from backups/wip/screen05-agents/ on top of the base). Nothing in the repository is changed.
set -e
REPO=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd); WS=${1:-/tmp/rainbow_r32}; V=$REPO/tools/marble05/viewer
mkdir -p "$WS/base"; cd "$WS/base"
cp -f "$V"/* . 2>/dev/null || true
[ -d node_modules/@sparkjsdev/spark ] || { npm init -y >/dev/null; npm install three@0.180.0 @sparkjsdev/spark@2.4.0 >/dev/null; }
ln -sf "$REPO/assets/models/benny31.glb" benny31.glb; ln -sf "$REPO/assets/textures/benny31/bake.png" bake.png; ln -sf "$REPO/assets/textures/paint/05_coin.png" coin.png
for f in full_500k full_100k full_full plus_500k; do [ -f "$REPO/qa/worldlabs/05/r32/$f.spz" ] && ln -sf "$REPO/qa/worldlabs/05/r32/$f.spz" "$f.spz"; done
[ -f "$REPO/qa/spaitial/05/echo2.spz" ] && ln -sf "$REPO/qa/spaitial/05/echo2.spz" echo2.spz
git -C "$REPO" lfs pull --include "qa/worldlabs/05/r32/*.spz,assets/models/benny31.glb" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
mkdir -p track
python3 -I "$REPO/tools/marble05/build_track.py" "$REPO/qa/worldlabs/05/r32/full_500k.spz" "$REPO/qa/worldlabs/05/r32/full_100k.spz" \

for f in near far bay bay_m bay_lo bay_m_lo; do ln -sf "track/$f.ply" "$f.ply"; done; ln -sf track/track.json track.json
for a in agentA agentB; do
  rm -rf "$WS/$a"; cp -a "$WS/base" "$WS/$a"
  [ -d "$REPO/backups/wip/screen05-agents/$a" ] && cp -a "$REPO/backups/wip/screen05-agents/$a/." "$WS/$a/"

done
echo "workspace ready: $WS (base, agentA, agentB). Stills: cd $WS/base && PAGE=play3.html STILLS='[0,2.3]' NODE_PATH=\$(npm root -g) node play_shots2.cjs out stills"

EOF

Here's the prompt to paste on your other account. Start the cloud session on branch **`claude/screen-05-3d-geometry-9yu7pu`** first, not the default branch:

```
Continue Rainbow round 32 exactly where the last account stopped. Read CLAUDE.md, then docs/briefs/2026-11-21-r32/RESUME_R32.md and docs/briefs/2026-11-21-r32/USER_R32.md (my binding orders). Run `bash docs/briefs/2026-11-21-r32/setup_r32.sh` to rebuild the Screen 05 3D workspace with both specialists' newest saved work (backups/wip/screen05-agents/). Relaunch the two specialists from AGENT_A_CONTROLS.md (animation-and-gameplay-engineer) and AGENT_B_WATER.md (water-fx-specialist) only if their notes show unfinished work, then merge, run the full real-swipe acceptance test (tools/marble05/viewer/final_acceptance.cjs + visual_check.py), fix and re-test until it passes. Do not show me a video until every test passes. No credits or purchases without my OK. Keep the five-minute GitHub autosave running.
```

**Comes along automatically**, because it's all in your GitHub repository:
- **Specialists:** all 10 specialist agents, with their instructions and saved work.
- **Tools:** the 3D track builder, gameplay page, acceptance test and visual checker. The setup command installs the 3D renderer and rebuilds the workspace.
- **Session hook:** the startup hook that restores everything and restarts the five-minute GitHub autosave.
- **History and assets:** all chat history, the 3D worlds, test videos, your rules and your approved artwork.

**Can't come along by itself.** These belong to your Claude account or cloud environment, not to the repository, so set them up once:
1. **World Labs (Marble) connector:** turn it on in claude.ai Settings → Connectors on the new account.
2. **Keys:** re-enter the World Labs and SpAItial keys only if the new Claude's free check says they're missing. It will open the secure form; never type a key in chat.
3. **Running specialists:** a running specialist can't move between accounts. The new session restarts them from their saved instructions and work, which the prompt above already tells it to do.

Your Marble credits (2,030) and SpAItial free credits (640) stay with your World Labs and SpAItial accounts, so they're still available from the new Claude account.
